title: Closed stabilizers and density
statement:
Let $S\subseteq V$ be a vector subspace. The stabilizer
$\operatorname{Stab}_{\operatorname{GL}(V)}(S)$ is Zariski closed.
Consequently $S$ is $\Pi$-stable if and only if it is
$H_{\mathrm{geom}}$-stable.

proof.text:
Choose a basis whose first vectors span $S$. The condition that a
matrix preserve $S$ says that each lower-left matrix entry is zero,
which is a finite list of polynomial equations. The stabilizer is
therefore closed. If $S$ is $\Pi$-stable, this closed stabilizer
contains $\rho(\Pi)$, hence contains its Zariski closure by
[def-wf-geometric-monodromy-group]; the converse is immediate.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $S\subseteq V=k^n$ be a vector subspace. The stabilizer
$\operatorname{Stab}_{\operatorname{GL}_n}(S)$ is Zariski closed.
Consequently, for a subgroup $\Gamma\subseteq\operatorname{GL}_n(k)$,
$S$ is $\Gamma$-stable if and only if it is stable under the Zariski
closure of $\Gamma$. In particular, for a represented degree datum
([d-monodromy]), $S$ is $P$-stable if and only if it is $H$-stable, and
$W$-stable if and only if it is $G$-stable.

proof.text:
Choose a basis whose first vectors span $S$. The condition that a
matrix preserve $S$ says that each lower-left matrix entry is zero,
which is a finite list of polynomial equations. The stabilizer is
therefore closed. If $S$ is $\Gamma$-stable, this closed stabilizer
contains $\Gamma$, hence contains its Zariski closure; the converse is
immediate. For a represented degree datum apply this to
$\Gamma=\rho(P)$ and $\Gamma=\rho(W)$, whose closures are $H$ and $G$ by
[d-monodromy].
